markdown:
## Why intent beats selectors

Classic browser automation hands an AI agent **selectors**: `#submit-btn`, `.product-row:nth-child(3)`. The moment the page renders differently — a redesigned dashboard, an A/B test, a tooltip overlay — the script breaks and the agent stops cold.

Skill Recorder ships **intent** instead: a markdown file that describes _what the human was trying to do_, with selectors as a fallback rather than the contract.

## The recording loop

When you click Start, Skill Recorder captures every event in real time:

- pointer clicks with semantic context (button text, ARIA labels, surrounding heading)
- keystroke groups (a 12-character typed value becomes one event, not 12)
- navigations and URL changes
- DOM snapshots at meaningful boundaries

At the end you have a faithful, replayable timeline. The interesting part is what happens next.

## Distillation, not transcription

A raw recording is too noisy to give an agent. The distillation step:

- collapses duplicate clicks into one
- promotes every typed value into a `{parameter}`
- detects auth boundaries and inserts a `Precondition: signed in` marker
- flags clicks on dynamic-list items with a ⚠️ warning so the agent knows the index might shift

The output is a SKILL.md the agent can read once and replay confidently.

## Hand-off

Drop the file into `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and Claude Code picks it up on next launch. The agent calls `browse skill <name> --arg1 value` and the flow runs end-to-end. No selectors to maintain. No glue code to write.
